title: sampled-telemetry-bundler-and-mini-runbook-compiler
author: Aisha Menon
description: Motivation: reduce on-call cognitive load and storage costs by sending compact, deterministic bundles of sampled telemetry for long-tail incidents and by compiling short-form runbooks (mini-runbooks) that only include the actionable steps and repro primitives. This PR adds a sampled telemetry bundler that implements configurable reservoir and time-decay sampling rules, a compact binary envelope for efficient transport and storage, and a mini-runbook compiler that extracts and compresses runbook deltas suitable for pager flows. The combined approach enables fast on-call context loads (sub-200ms deserialisation), smaller artifact footprints for postmortems, and fewer noisy notifications. Changes include a new sampling policy DSL, a telemetry bundler library (Go) with CLI, a mini-runbook compiler (Python) that consumes runbook templates and produces a concise execution plan, integration glue for the slo-toolkit agent to attach bundles to alerts, and end-to-end e2e tests. Backwards compatibility: full-size telemetry and full runbooks are still supported; sampling and mini-runbook generation are opt-in via a feature flag per-service. Rollout plan: alpha on internal infra teams for 2 weeks, canary to 10% of customers via SLO config UI, then gradual ramp; metrics to monitor: bundle size, bundle generation latency, deserialization time on mobile/web clients, oncall resolution time, and false-negative rate for missing context. Security: bundles are signed with the existing KMS adapter; no PII is added by default and redaction rules are applied during bundling. See linked linear items for UX and rollout details.
